Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 26-year-old female with new onset dry, itchy, red skin primarily on hands and arms, beginning a few days ago after swimming. No fever, no vomiting, normal appetite and bowel/urinary function. Reports tiredness. No prior eczema or dermatitis. Family history of atopy (asthma, hayfever).  
- Clinical impression (per transcript): Dermatitis.  
- Differential considerations consistent with DDx:
  - Irritant contact dermatitis (likely related to chlorine/pool chemicals or soaps/handwashing) given onset after swimming and distribution to hands/arms.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis to pool chemicals or personal care products.
  - Atopic dermatitis (adult-onset) less likely but possible given family atopy and stress as a trigger.  
- No examination or labs performed/documented.

Management Plan
-  Topical therapy: Prescribe/advise use of steroid cream (strength not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented) and regular emollients to dry areas throughout the day.  
- Symptom relief: OTC antihistamines (e.g., Piriton, Loratadine) for itch.  
- Education: Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis.  
- Analgesia: Paracetamol/painkillers not expected to help for itch.  
- Follow-up: Return if not improving within 1 week for reassessment.

- Irritant contact dermatitis (High): Temporal link to swimming; hands/arms involvement; dry, itchy, red skin; no systemic symptoms.  
- Allergic contact dermatitis (Moderate): Possible reaction to pool chemicals or personal care products; pruritic erythema on exposed areas.  
- Atopic dermatitis, adult-onset (Moderate): Family atopy and stress may predispose; first episode at age 26 and onset post-exposure make contact dermatitis more likely.
